blocks.text: Gross margin expanded by 0.6 pp to 46.9%. Revenue grew faster than the direct cost of goods — usually pricing power, a richer product/service mix, scale purchasing or lower input costs. EBITDA margin rose 0.1 pp. Stripping out the gross-margin effect, operating expenses (selling, admin, R&D) cost 0.5 pp — overheads grew faster than revenue (investment in growth, wage inflation, marketing, or falling sales against fixed costs). Net margin rose 2.9 pp. Items below EBITDA (depreciation, interest, tax, one-offs) helped by 2.8 pp — e.g. lower interest cost, a lower tax rate or a one-time gain. Operating leverage this year: EBITDA +5.8% on revenue +10.9% = 0.53×. Profits are growing slower than sales — costs are catching up. Gross-margin range over 5 years: 41.8%–46.9% (volatile — sensitive to costs, pricing or cycle). DuPont: ROE 19.0% ≈ net margin 26.9% × asset turnover 1.25× × equity multiplier 0.60×. Driven mainly by high profitability. ROIC of 0.1% is below a typical cost of capital — growth at these returns destroys value.
